title: SKU pricing & headcount realignment - May 2026
body:
Executive summary:
This sheet is a proposal for a short-cycle headcount realignment tied to SKU pricing changes for May–Sep 2026. Goal: preserve gross margin targets (target 58% blended gross margin) while keeping time-to-hire and critical SRE/serving-runtime hires on track. We model three pricing sensitivity lanes and resulting recommended hiring phasing and temporary role repurposes.

Key assumptions (clean, traffic-agnostic):
- Three SKUs: Starter (S), Scale (M), Enterprise (E).
- Baseline SKU prices (current): S=$0.0009/req, M=$0.0028/req, E=$0.010/req.
- Baseline GPU-hour cost (weighted across fleet): $4.80/GPU-hour.
- Average requests per GPU-hour by SKU (effective concurrency): S=2.6k req/hr, M=5.4k req/hr, E=22k req/hr.
- Headcount cost per FTE (loaded fully-burdened): Eng IC $220k/year, SRE $240k/year, Solutions Eng $190k/year, Finance/PM $160k/year.
- Hiring lead times: Eng 9–12 weeks, SRE 10–14 weeks, Solutions Eng 6–8 weeks.
- Hiring freeze or temporary repurpose triggers defined below.

Baseline monthly run-rate (illustrative):
CSV:Month,Revenue,Opex (ex-HC),Headcount Cost,Total OpEx,Gross Margin
CSV:May-2026,$3,100,000,$680,000,$1,045,000,$1,725,000,58%

Headcount plan (baseline vs adaptive):
CSV:Role,Baseline FTEs (EoQ2),Planned Hires (May-Sep),Adaptive Plan Notes
CSV:Serving Runtime Engineers,18,4,Delay 2 hires to Aug if revenue < 90% baseline
CSV:SRE,6,2,Convert 1 infra eng (6w) to cross-train for on-call if price pressure
CSV:Solutions Eng,10,3,Defer 1 hire and shift to customer self-serve enablement
CSV:Finance/PM,4,1,No change

Pricing sensitivity lanes (scenario definitions):
- Baseline: prices unchanged.
- Down-15%: discretionary price compression (competitive pressure) lowers realized SKU price by 15% uniform; elastic demand assumed +4% volume (materially small).
- Up-10%: targeted price uplift on Enterprise SKU only (+10%) with negligible demand elasticity.

Scenario impacts (high-level):
CSV:Scenario,Delta Price (blended),Projected Revenue,Projected Gross Margin,Hiring Recommendation
CSV:Baseline,0%,$3.10M,58%,Proceed with hires per baseline
CSV:Down-15%,-15%,$2.68M,48% (approx),Pause 2 eng hires; repurpose 1 infra contractor
CSV:Up-10% (E only),+4% blended,$3.22M,61%,Accelerate SRE hire; proceed with others

Explanation of the margin math (short):
- We compute realized revenue = baseline revenue * (1 + blended price delta).
- GPU-costs are treated as variable and scale with volume (approx linear). For downside we keep GPU-hour efficiency constant; downside margin compression is mainly from lower realized price.
- Headcount is semi-fixed; we show the near-term levers: delay hires, shift contractors, temporary role repurposes to preserve SLA while reducing burn.

Trigger matrix (operational):
- If realized revenue for rolling 14 days falls below 93% of plan -> trigger hiring pause on non-critical Eng hires.
- If realized revenue falls below 88% -> freeze all external contractors and start monthly site-capacity audits; escalate to CFO for pricing and sales interventions.
- If net gross margin drops below 50% for 2 consecutive weeks -> engage Product to push enterprise price uplift pilot.

Stress-case micro-actions (what to do immediately on price shock):
1) Reassign 1 backend eng to infra on-call for 6 weeks (low rework cost).
2) Suspend non-critical infra projects (e.g., telemetry expansions) to free SRE cycles.
3) Introduce a temporary Enterprise SKU surcharge (opt-in) with immediate go-to-customer comms; track uptake.
4) Offer limited-time prepaid capacity credits (tightened discounts) to improve cash and reduce price decay.

Five-month cash / headcount phasing (compact view):
CSV:Month,Net Cash Burn (proj),New Hires Started,Hiring Paused Flag
CSV:May-2026,$1,020,000,2,false
CSV:Jun-2026,$1,140,000,1,false
CSV:Jul-2026,$980,000,2,false
CSV:Aug-2026,$1,150,000,3,false
CSV:Sep-2026,$1,010,000,1,false

Sensitivity table (blended price delta vs required HC cut to maintain 58% margin):
CSV:Blended Price Delta,Revenue Impact,HQ Cut Required (FTEs),Operational Notes
CSV:-20%,-20%,-6 (FTEs),Immediate hiring pause + 3 contractor swaps
CSV:-15%,-14%,-4 (FTEs),Delay 2 eng hires + reassign 1 contractor
CSV:-10%,-10%,-2 (FTEs),Delay 1 eng hire, reprioritize projects
CSV:-5%,-5%,0,Friendly to run through seasonal variance
CSV:+5%,+5%,+1 (FTE),Add 1 Solutions Eng to accelerate land

Open questions / unknowns (short list):
- True elasticity by SKU — our +4% for -15% price is an initial heuristic; need customer-level telemetry by SKU to refine.
- Impact of quantization/tech ops savings on GPU-hour cost profile not yet quantified in this model; potential upside if adoption accelerates.
- Time-to-hire volatility in SF vs remote hires; sensitivity to candidate market not modeled.

Action items (next 10 business days):
- Finance: finalize blended GPU-hour cost by May 8 (Evan).
- Eng leads: identify two non-critical projects to pause if downward pressure occurs (Sofia).
- Sales & Solutions: prepare an enterprise targeted +10% uplift pilot and customer messaging (Liam).
- Prod/Applied ML: supply SKU-level per-GPU efficiency measurements for May 1–May 31 (ask via ticket ENG-4821).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on hiring lead-times and optimistic on enterprise price uplift uptake. Treat numbers as illustrative for board-level discussion on May 18.
- If reviewers want an alternate sensitivity that ties price delta to variable GPU efficiency (i.e., assume better batching reduces GPU-hours when price drops), flag and finance will produce v2.

Appendix: small calculation snippet (example):
- Effective revenue per GPU-hour (S) = price_per_request * requests_per_gpu_hour -> $0.0009 * 2600 = $2.34/GPU-hour (starter)
- Effective revenue per GPU-hour (M) = $0.0028 * 5400 = $15.12/GPU-hour (scale)
- Effective revenue per GPU-hour (E) = $0.010 * 22000 = $220/GPU-hour (enterprise)
- Blended effective revenue per GPU-hour (baseline) = weighted avg across volume mix -> used for margin calcs.

End of sheet.

Comments/edits: please add inline comments in the sheet cells and ping finance slack #fin-models when you update numbers.
